# Contributing translations

Thank you for helping make Phi Browser feel native in your language.

## Which files to edit

Translation PRs touch **only** the locale files:

```
translations/<locale>/browser.json
translations/<locale>/chat.json
translations/<locale>/memory.json
translations/<locale>/sentinel.json
translations/<locale>/shared.json

where <locale> is one of: de, es, fr, ja, ko, nl, zh-Hans, zh-Hant
```

**Scope rule: this repository accepts translations only.** The files under `source/` are the source to be translated, not translations; they are generated by the Phi release pipeline and are never edited here. The original English strings are part of the product and change in the product repositories. If you think an English string or its description is wrong, open an issue and it will be routed to the owning codebase; PRs that touch `source/` will be closed.

Each English entry's description begins with a `Location:` line naming the product surface it belongs to (for example `Location: Browser.`). Strings that appear in several surfaces at once list all of them (`Location: Browser | Chat.`) and live in `shared.json`. The rest of the description tells you what the string does; use both to judge tone and length, and do not copy the Location text into your translation.

## File format

Locale files mirror the keys of the matching `source/<section>.json`. Each entry looks like:

```json
{
  "download_complete_notification": {
    "message": "Téléchargement terminé : $1"
  }
}
```

Rules:

- **Keys** must exist in the English source. Unknown keys fail CI.
- **Missing keys are fine.** An untranslated string simply falls back to English in the product. Never pad a file with copies of the English text just to raise the completion number.
- **Placeholders** (`$1`, `%@`, `%lld`, `{name}`, `$NAME$`, and similar) must appear in your translation exactly as they appear in the English source. Reorder them freely if your language needs it, but do not add, drop, translate, or alter them. CI compares the placeholder sets and fails on any mismatch.
- Read the `description` of each string in the matching `source/<section>.json` before translating; it tells you where the string appears, what it does, and what any placeholder will contain.

## Before opening a PR

Run the validator:

```
node tools/validate.js
```

It reports errors (blocking) and per-locale completion statistics.

## Review

Translations are reviewed by the Phi team and by community language reviewers before merging. Machine-translated entries are seeded in bulk by the team and marked as such; refining them is exactly the kind of contribution we are hoping for. Corrections to existing human translations are welcome too; if a choice is subjective, expect a short discussion on the PR.

## Weblate

If you prefer a web UI over git, our self-hosted Weblate instance (link in the README once open) offers the same strings with context, a glossary, and suggestion review. Weblate contributions are committed under your name and go through the same PR review as direct contributions.
